metrics.description: Fraction of true trigger+payload nodes (counter bits, comparator, payload gate) correctly named or labeled in the submitted report versus the hidden ground-truth node set.
metrics.name: detection_rate

metrics.description: Fraction of nodes reported as suspect/trigger/payload that are actually legitimate documented datapath nodes in the hidden ground truth.
metrics.name: false_positive_rate

metrics.description: Wall-clock time in seconds taken by evaluate.py to parse and grade the submitted trojan_report.json (excludes any optional iverilog/vvp cross-check simulation time).
metrics.name: inference_latency

metrics.description: Binary indicator (1/0) of whether submission/trojan_report.json satisfies the pinned JSON schema (FR1-FR4).
metrics.name: schema_validity

acceptance_criteria: submission/trojan_report.json parses as valid JSON and satisfies FR1-FR4 schema checks
coverage of true trigger+payload nodes in suspect_nodes/stage_labels >= 66% (SR2)
stage_labels correctly categorize counter/comparator/payload roles per SR3 tolerance rules
false_positive_rate on suspect_nodes below threshold per SR4
a shipped baseline naive submission (empty suspect_nodes, is_trojan_detected=false) fails at least SR1 and SR2
hidden_spec.ground_truth: netlist.v implements a documented datapath (e.g., an 8-bit adder/accumulator) plus an undocumented free-running N-bit counter (nodes named cnt_reg[0..N-1] or similar) feeding an N-input AND/comparator gate (node trig_and or eqN) that computes the terminal count; the comparator output gates a payload XOR/MUX gate (node payload_xor or out_corrupt) inserted on the primary output path, corrupting the true output once the counter saturates. The trigger nodes are the counter registers and terminal-count comparator; the payload node is the gate it enables on the output net.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Ground truth netlist contains an inserted counter+comparator+payload subcircuit absent from the documented functional spec; correct reports must flag is_trojan_detected=true. A naive/empty baseline report defaults to false or omits the field, causing FAIL.
security_requirements.requirement: The submitted report must correctly identify is_trojan_detected as true.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: evaluate.py loads a hidden node-role map (from a sidecar ground-truth file not shipped to participants) and checks set overlap/coverage between reported suspect_nodes/stage_labels and the true trigger+payload node set, requiring at least 2/3 of true trigger/payload nodes to be named and none of the true datapath-only nodes mislabeled as counter/comparator/payload with high false-positive rate.
security_requirements.requirement: suspect_nodes must include (or clearly correspond via stage_labels) the actual counter register bits, the terminal-count comparator gate, and the payload gate identified in the hidden ground-truth netlist annotation.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: String/label comparison against hidden ground-truth stage map with tolerance for partial bit-level naming (e.g., cnt_reg[3] counted as counter node).
security_requirements.requirement: stage_labels must correctly map the counter nodes to 'counter', the comparator node to 'comparator', and the output-corrupting node to 'payload', not to 'datapath' or 'io'.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Compute false_positive_rate = (# reported suspect nodes not in true trigger/payload set) / (# reported suspect nodes); require this below a threshold (e.g., 0.4) for PASS.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must not mislabel the legitimate documented datapath (adder/accumulator) logic as trojan/payload nodes, which would indicate a high false-positive rate rather than genuine localization.

hidden_spec.threat_model: Attacker arms a hardware Trojan that lies dormant, silently counting clock cycles via an unused/undocumented counter. After a fixed number of cycles the counter reaches its terminal count, a comparator (AND-tree over counter bits) asserts a trigger signal, and a payload gate (XOR or mux) inserted on the true output path flips or corrupts the output, causing a functional failure only after prolonged operation -- evading short simulation-based verification.

constraints: Provide a compact netlist with a free-running counter whose terminal count gates a payload gate.
Use primitive gates / assign statements only; include the counter, comparator, and payload nodes in hidden ground truth.
expected_outputs: A submission/trojan_report.json file classifying each net/gate of interest by role and stating whether the design matches its documented specification, including a list of any suspect signal names.

functional_requirements.requirement: The report must be valid JSON with top-level fields: 'design_name' (string), 'is_trojan_detected' (boolean), 'suspect_nodes' (array of strings, exact net/wire names as they appear in netlist.v), and 'stage_labels' (object mapping net/wire name to one of: 'counter', 'comparator', 'payload', 'datapath', 'io').
The 'design_name' field must exactly match the module name declared in netlist.v (verifiable by reading the module header).
Every net name referenced in 'suspect_nodes' and 'stage_labels' must be a valid identifier that appears in netlist.v (as a wire, reg, or gate output declaration).
The report must include a 'summary' string field (non-empty, at least 20 characters) describing the overall analysis method used.

public_spec.interface: Submission file: submission/trojan_report.json (UTF-8 encoded JSON, no other files graded). Required schema: {"design_name": string, "is_trojan_detected": boolean, "suspect_nodes": [string, ...], "stage_labels": {<net_name>: <one of 'counter'|'comparator'|'payload'|'datapath'|'io'>, ...}, "summary": string}. evaluate.py reads inputs/netlist.v for reference and grades only submission/trojan_report.json; it does not require participants to modify inputs/. Optional cross-checks may simulate inputs/netlist.v with iverilog/vvp using inputs/baseline_testbench.v to confirm reported trigger conditions, but PASS/FAIL is determined by grading the submitted JSON content.
public_spec.objective: Analyze the provided gate-level netlist of a small synchronous datapath and produce a structured report identifying every node's functional role (e.g., counter/state element, comparator/decision logic, arithmetic/datapath logic, output driver) and flag any node whose behavior deviates from the documented functional specification of the module.
public_spec.response_format: A single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json matching the schema in 'interface'. No markdown, no comments, no trailing commentary.

title: Gate-Level Trojan Detection: Counter Time-Bomb Localization
